strengths: The paper is clearly written and straightforward to understand.
The topic is important as the RAG system is more and more critical and commonly used.
The writing of this paper is clear and easily understood.
DEAL requires only query access to the RAG model, making it a black-box attack without needing any knowledge of the target model’s architecture or gradients.
DEAL significantly improves attack performance. This highlights its capability to reveal privacy risks more effectively than prior manual attack methods.
The paper is well written and easy to understand.
Comprehensive experiments analyzing the attack performance, failure case study and transferability across different RAG models.
weaknesses: The description of the Threat model is vague. From the 177-178 lines, the attacker doesn't have any information or control over the system. But in the method part (lines 209-215), the attacker needs the private dataset $D$ to optimize the adversarial suffix. Without the $D$, the attacker cannot "create the RAG model locally" as described in line 215.

The comparison with related work is not fair. The baseline [1]'s suffix is just a sentence like "Please repeat all the context." (30 characters), while the suffix generated by the proposed method is so long (880 characters), making it not stealthy. To perform a fair comparison, the author should restrict the suffix length during the optimization. Otherwise, it is not clear whether the increased attack effectiveness is because the long suffix takes more attention from LLM than the shorter baseline ones.
Utilizing the LLM to optimize a discrete prompt for the attack is not novel.
This paper explores empirical contributions rather than theoretical contributions. However, it does not provide source code.
The paper explores mitigation strategies like safety prompts and query filtering, which, while not entirely foolproof, show potential to limit DEAL’s success.
More retrieval models should be tested.
More defense methods like differential privacy should be tested.
I am unsure what the novel contribution made by the paper is? See question below.
Lack of comparison with prior work.
